rice.label: Rice
rice.text: Plain white rice. It forgives a lot.

noodles.label: Noodles
noodles.text: Wheat noodles, dried, from a good packet.

flour.label: Flour
flour.text: For dough, pancakes and everything that needs a base.

rice_paper.label: Rice Paper
rice_paper.text: Thin round sheets, dry as old letters. One second in warm water.

cabbage.label: Cabbage
cabbage.text: A tight green head from Nonna's garden.

chicken_meat.label: Chicken
chicken_meat.text: From a hen that had a name.

pork.label: Pork
pork.text: Dark, well-marbled, from a Cinta Senese pig.

beef.label: Beef
beef.text: From a dark Pisana. Slow and generous.

eggs.label: Eggs
eggs.text: Still warm, if you were quick.

truffle.label: Truffle
truffle.text: Found by a pig with excellent priorities.

zucchini.label: Zucchini
zucchini.text: Long, green, and always more than you asked for.

salmon_steak.label: Salmon Steaks, raw
salmon_steak.text: Not a local fish. Nonna's cousin sends it from the north.

tofu.label: Tofu
tofu.text: White, firm, pressed this morning. It tastes of almost nothing until you teach it.

wildkraeuter.label: Wild Herbs
wildkraeuter.text: Thyme, myrtle and sage from the maquis.

lemongrass.label: Lemongrass
lemongrass.text: Smells of lemon and tastes of somewhere else. It likes Nonna's soil.

tomaten.label: Tomatoes
tomaten.text: Sun-warm and a little too ripe.

milk.label: Milk
milk.text: Whole milk, still cool from the cow.

knoblauch.label: Garlic
knoblauch.text: A braid of bulbs. Vampires and cowards stay away.

zitronen.label: Lemons
zitronen.text: From the terraces above the cove.

sojasauce.label: Soy Sauce
sojasauce.text: Dark and salty. Smells like the kitchen at home.

fish_sauce.label: Fish Sauce
fish_sauce.text: Amber and salty. Everybody says it stinks. Everybody comes back.

sea_bass_roh.label: Sea Bass Fillets, raw
sea_bass_roh.text: From the european sea bass: silvery and shy, it hides near the rocks of the bay.

gilt_head_bream_roh.label: Bream Fillets, raw
gilt_head_bream_roh.text: From the gilt-head bream: recognised by the golden band between its eyes.

red_mullet_roh.label: Red Mullet Fillets, raw
red_mullet_roh.text: From the red mullet: pink-red, with two whiskers it uses to feel the sand.

scorpionfish_roh.label: Rascasse for the Pot, raw
scorpionfish_roh.text: From the scorpionfish: ugly as sin, wonderful in a bouillabaisse.

sardine_roh.label: Sardine Fillets, raw
sardine_roh.text: From the sardine: small, silver, and everywhere in summer.

salmon_roh.label: Salmon Fillets, raw
salmon_roh.text: From the atlantic salmon: silver and strong. Nobody knows what it is doing this far south.

cuttlefish_roh.label: Cuttlefish Strips, raw
cuttlefish_roh.text: From the cuttlefish: it changes colour when it is curious.

octopus_roh.label: Octopus Tentacle, raw
octopus_roh.text: From the common octopus: clever hands, eight of them.

red_prawn_roh.label: Peeled Red Prawns, raw
red_prawn_roh.text: From the red prawn: from the deep water off the cape, red even before cooking.

spiny_lobster_roh.label: Lobster Tail, raw
spiny_lobster_roh.text: From the spiny lobster: no claws, but a crown of spines. A festa fish.

brown_trout_roh.label: Trout Fillets, raw
brown_trout_roh.text: From the mediterranean trout: spotted like the stones in its stream.

eel_roh.label: Eel Pieces, raw
eel_roh.text: From the european eel: slippery and old. Some say it is older than the village.

carp_roh.label: Carp Steaks, raw
carp_roh.text: From the common carp: slow, wide and patient, like the river itself.

pike_roh.label: Pike Fillets, raw
pike_roh.text: From the northern pike: a long green hunter that waits in the reeds.

perch_roh.label: Perch Fillets, raw
perch_roh.text: From the european perch: striped like a tiny tiger, with a red fin.

tench_roh.label: Tench Fillets, raw
tench_roh.text: From the tench: the quiet doctor fish of the slow pools.

barbel_roh.label: Barbel Fillets, raw
barbel_roh.text: From the barbel: it feeds along the stony bottom with four whiskers.

zander_roh.label: Zander Fillets, raw
zander_roh.text: From the zander: pike-perch: firm white meat, shy eyes.

river_crayfish_roh.label: Crayfish Tails, raw
river_crayfish_roh.text: From the river crayfish: a small armoured fighter under the river stones.

river_crab_roh.label: River Crab Meat, raw
river_crab_roh.text: From the river crab: the sweet little crab of the Italian streams.

pig.label: Pig

cow.label: Cow

frederico.text: I'll bring it over right now, Officer! Well... right after the goat finishes her lunch. She's very particular.
frederico.gesprochen: I'll bring it over right now, Officer! [chuckle] Well... right after the goat finishes her lunch. She's very particular.

frederico.text: It'll be there before you've even said goodbye. Okay, maybe a little after. The cart has a wobbly wheel.
frederico.gesprochen: It'll be there before you've even said goodbye. [laugh] Okay, maybe a little after. The cart has a wobbly wheel.

frederico.text: Nonna says I must carry it carefully. I have never dropped anything. Only once. Twice, if you count Tuesday.
frederico.gesprochen: Nonna says I must carry it carefully. [sniff] I have never dropped anything. Only once. Twice, if you count Tuesday.

frederico.text: I'll run all the way! Almost all the way. The hill is very steep, and the goat has opinions.
frederico.gesprochen: I'll run all the way! [gasp] Almost all the way. The hill is very steep, and the goat has opinions.

frederico.text: Your shopping is in good hands, Officer. Small hands, but fast ones.
frederico.gesprochen: Your shopping is in good hands, Officer. [chuckle] Small hands, but fast ones.

frederico.text: I'll put it in the kitchen myself and I won't peek. Only a little peek. At the cheese.
frederico.gesprochen: I'll put it in the kitchen myself and I won't peek. [laugh] Only a little peek. At the cheese.

frederico.text: Leave it to me! That's what Nonna says right before she gives me more work. But I like it.
frederico.gesprochen: Leave it to me! [cough] That's what Nonna says right before she gives me more work. But I like it.

frederico.text: Goodbye, Officer! The cart and I are faster than the weather. Usually.
frederico.gesprochen: Goodbye, Officer! The cart and I are faster than the weather. [chuckle] Usually.

timber.label: Timber
timber.text: Split logs from the valley, stacked to dry. They smell better than anything you'll ever build with them.

slate.label: Slate
slate.text: Dark plates split from the ridges above Corte. The old roofs here wear it. It breaks along its own grain, never along yours.

granite.label: Granite
granite.text: Grey, speckled and in no hurry. The island is made of it, and so is every wall still standing after a winter.

iron.label: Iron Fittings
iron.text: Hinges, nails and brackets from the smith in Corte.

cork.label: Cork
cork.text: Bark from a cork oak, light and warm to the touch. Petru carves floats from it.

feather.label: Gull Feather
feather.text: A stiff grey-white feather, clean as paper. Petru ties them onto his best lures.

cloth.label: Cloth
cloth.text: A bolt of plain linen that fell off a ferry, according to the man who sold it. It still smells of the ferry.

wool.label: Corsican Wool
wool.text: Rough, oily and warm, straight off a mountain sheep. It keeps out everything except the smell of sheep.

leather.label: Boar Leather
leather.text: Thick hide with a few old scars in it. The boar had a hard life, and the leather remembers.

coral.label: Red Coral
coral.text: A branch of red coral from the rocks off the Punta d'Orsu. A good tailor can get six buttons out of it. A bad one gets four.

steel.label: Steel
steel.text: Nobody on this island makes it. It only comes ashore inside the machines sent to find you, so you take it back out.

chicken.text: A small henhouse with one perch row.
A bigger run and a second perch row: room for three more.
Nesting boxes full of straw: every hen lays one more egg, and chicks come sooner.

pig.text: A stone sty under the chestnut trees.
A fenced oak grove next door: room for two more.
A muddy wallow and the deep oak wood: the pigs find one more truffle, and piglets come sooner.

cow.text: A second stall row and a water trough: room for two more.
A summer pasture on the terraces: every cow gives one more milk, and calves come sooner.

boot.label: Fishing off the Swim Platform
boot.text: Rod, bucket, the stern in the shade. The sea doesn't hurry.

meer.label: Driftwood
meer.text: A bleached plank, still good wood.

meer.label: Rusty Anchor Chain
meer.text: A length of old chain. The smith will want it.

meer.label: Gull Feather
meer.text: A grey-white feather caught in the rocks. Petru would know what to do with it.

meer.label: Red Coral
meer.text: A branch of red coral tangled in your line. Somebody on the island will want that.

fluss.label: River Slate
fluss.text: A handful of thin flat plates from the bottom.

fluss.label: Waterlogged Branch
fluss.text: A heavy oak branch. It'll dry.

meer.label: Lea's Lucky Lure
meer.text: Lea saw your journal and pressed her grandad's old lure into your hand. The golden band stays a little wider.

fluss.label: Petru's Cork Float
fluss.text: Petru turned your journal page by page and gave you a cork float he carved himself. The golden band stays a little wider.

stufen.label: Old Hatchet
stufen.text: His father's hatchet. Not sharp, but it has never let go of the handle.

stufen.label: Forester's Axe
stufen.text: A new head on a hickory handle. One clean stroke per tree.

stufen.label: Tempered Axe
stufen.text: Petru forged it and Rosi hardened the steel. The tree simply comes down.

stufen.label: Old Pick
stufen.text: Heavy, blunt and honest. The rock decides when it breaks.

stufen.label: Quarry Pick
stufen.text: Freshly forged points. One good blow and the rock splits.

stufen.label: Tempered Pick
stufen.text: Tempered twice by Rosi. The stone gives way before you finish the swing.

cork_float.label: Cork Float
cork_float.text: A round float carved from oak bark, painted by hand. It doesn't do much. It does it every time.

balsa_float.label: Balsa Float
balsa_float.text: A slim balsa float with a gull's feather in the varnish. The golden band is wider and the better fish come closer.

wooden_lure.label: Wooden Lure
wooden_lure.text: A little wooden fish with a diving lip and two silver hooks. It swims like something alive, and the fish are not clever about that.

fisch_notiz.sea_bass: The French call him the sea wolf. He hunts in the white water where the waves break, when it is too rough for anyone sensible. There are plenty in the bay, so the price is small.
fisch_notiz.gilt_head_bream: See the gold between the eyes? That's how you know her. She cracks mussels with those teeth, so the meat is sweet, but half the harbour catches her, and I can't pay much.
fisch_notiz.red_mullet: Two whiskers to taste the sand with. The Romans paid silver for this fish, they say. Today I pay you a few coins, and that is how the world goes.
fisch_notiz.scorpionfish: Careful with the spines, they sting worse than a wasp. Ugly fish. But without him there is no real bouillabaisse, so I pay you a fair price.
fisch_notiz.sardine: Sardines come in their thousands every summer, so nobody pays much for one. Grill it with salt and eat it with your fingers. On this coast that is still the best supper there is.
fisch_notiz.salmon: A salmon, here? He must have lost his way to the north. They say he finds the river he was born in by the smell, after years at sea. I pay fair for a fish that far from home.
fisch_notiz.cuttlefish: She changes colour while you watch her, when she's afraid and when she's curious. The ink turns rice black, and the bone inside goes to the birds. A fair price for all of that.
fisch_notiz.octopus: Hm. Clever animal. Bastianu, at my workshop, opens jars when I'm not looking. Don't tell him I bought this one. Fair price.
fisch_notiz.red_prawn: From the deep water off the cape, where the light never reaches. Red before it ever sees a pan. The restaurants in Bastia fight over these, so I pay you well.
fisch_notiz.spiny_lobster: No claws, only spines and those long whips. Hold him close to your ear, he creaks when he's angry. Weddings, baptisms, festas: for him I pay the best price I have.
fisch_notiz.brown_trout: A trout from the cold water up high. Look at the spots, every stream paints them a little differently. The hills are full of streams, though, so I can't pay much.
fisch_notiz.eel: Every eel in this river was born on the other side of the ocean, and one day she swims all the way back. Nobody has ever seen where. I pay well for a traveller like that.
fisch_notiz.carp: The monks kept carp in their ponds for the fasting days. Slow fish, and he lives longer than most dogs. He tastes of mud if you cook him wrong, so the price is small.
fisch_notiz.pike: He waits in the reeds without moving, an hour if he has to, and then he takes a duckling off the water. Mind the teeth, they point backwards. Fair price.
fisch_notiz.perch: Stripes like a small tiger, and a fin that bites back if you grab him wrong. Where there is one, there are twenty. So, not much money.
fisch_notiz.tench: The doctor fish. The old men say the others rub against him when they are sick, because of the slime. I don't know if it's true. Cheap, but honest.
fisch_notiz.barbel: Four whiskers, and he reads the riverbed with them like a blind man reads a face. Don't eat the eggs, they'll keep you in bed for two days. A fair price for a fair fish.
fisch_notiz.zander: The zander. Eyes like a cat, so he hunts at night while the others sleep. Firm white meat, no mud in it at all. I pay you well for him.
fisch_notiz.river_crayfish: He only lives where the water is clean. When the crayfish leave a stream, something upstream is wrong. I pay fair for good news like that.
fisch_notiz.river_crab: A crab that has never seen the sea. At night he climbs out and sits on the warm stones like an old man. Hm. Odd neighbour. Fair price.
